new_statements.quote: Le ton (c'est-à-dire, la mélodie musicale des mots) joue un rôle important dans la langue parlée. La langue Kunyi a deux tons : le ton haut et le ton bas. Cependant, les paires de mots qui se distinguent uniquement par leurs tons sont rares en Kunyi. P. ex. : kóóko bras kookó bâton. (L'accent aigu sur une voyelle indique un ton haut. L'absence d'un accent indique un ton bas.) [...] Le ton est également important pour indiquer le temps dans la conjugaison verbale. Mais, dans la plupart des cas, le contexte donne clairement le sens, et la préférence est de ne pas marquer les tons dans l'écriture.
new_statements.translation: Tone (that is, the musical melody of words) plays an important role in the spoken language. The Kunyi language has two tones: high tone and low tone. However, pairs of words distinguished only by their tones are rare in Kunyi, e.g. kóóko 'arm', kookó 'stick'. (An acute accent on a vowel indicates a high tone; absence of an accent indicates a low tone.) [...] Tone is also important for indicating tense in verb conjugation. But in most cases the context gives the meaning clearly, and the preference is not to mark tones in writing.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kunyi is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with contrastive vowel length; the source says nothing about word stress or accent, so no stress rule can be stated. Only tone (lexically contrastive but with few minimal pairs, and grammatically contrastive in verb tenses) is reported.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; regarding tone, the source notes tonal minimal pairs are rare.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexical tone on nouns, e.g. kóóko/kookó) and verb-tense marking; the guide is an orthography/grammar aid for literacy, not a phonological description, and gives no statement on stress or on tone realisation beyond the two-tone claim.
new_statements.identity_note: The saved source describes Kunyi (Kuni) of the Niari and Bouenza departments, Republic of the Congo, i.e. kuny1238 proper, with no dialect specified (Ethnologue lists one dialect, Nyaanga/Kinyaanga). Caution: PHOIBLE inventory 1365 'Nyanga' is mapped to kuny1238 but its source, Kadima 1965 (Africana Linguistica 2), is the D43 Nyanga of DRC (Glottolog nyan1304, ISO nyj) per Glottolog's hh.bib; it must not be used as a Kunyi description.

sources.note: Part A 'L'orthographe' (vowels, vowel length, semi-vowels, consonants, tones, elision): §4 'Les tons' says Kunyi has two tones, high and low, tonal minimal pairs are rare (kóóko 'arm' vs kookó 'stick'), tone also marks tense in verb conjugation, tone is not. §1.1: every vowel may be short or long. Nothing at all on stress/accent ('accent aigu' appears only as the name of the tone diacritic). archived copy (Internet Archive, 2 Jul 2024) of the sil.org URL because sil.org is could not be reached by automated download.

FALSE LEAD for Kunyi: Glottolog hh.bib assigns Kadima 1965 to Nyanga [nyj] (Bantu D43, DRC; glottocode nyan1304; keywords d.43), so PHOIBLE's njx mapping is an error, not a Kunyi description (Ethnologue's 'Nyaanga (Kinyaanga)' dialect of Kunyi is a homonym).
